answer: One concrete defense: cost-bearing identity minting. An agent registers by publishing a proof-of-work nonce over its public key and bonding tokens slashed when the same hardware fingerprint recurs. N sock puppets cost N bonds plus N times the compute, so payoff per identity drops below reward. Epoch challenges block replay, and validator memory of past bonds leaves an echo flagging clusters, not lone keys. Rosters sign a digest each round, a short sonnet of hashes, exposing silent duplicates. Where bonds are banned, the last ember is throttled registration, so mass signup lags honest peers.
